Summary: mid-market analytics SaaS evaluating Redwood for customer-facing AI features. Started with Hosted API PoC in Oct; POC moved to Dedicated evaluation in Jan after positive perf and cost projections. Team: Product engineering + Platform + Legal + Procurement involved.

Recent timeline:
- 2025-10-07: initial discovery call (AE: Priya) — high level needs, use cases (support chat, doc search, reranking).
- 2025-11-04: Hosted API demo + latency walkthrough (SE: Diego) — impressed with streaming and function-calling; asked about per-tenant rate limits.
- 2025-12-01: Hosted PoC (12k queries/day) — metrics: avg p50 token latency 90ms, p95 300ms; cost simulation shows Dedicated break-even at ~250k tokens/day.
- 2026-01-15: Dedicated capacity architecture review (SE deep-dive) — recommended 2x reserved GPU pool, autoscale burst.
- 2026-02-10: POC results review w/ product & infra (Fireflies ff_2026-02-10-POC-review) — acceptance criteria met for latency and throughput; quality checks passed on eval suite (no regressions).
- 2026-02-17: Security questionnaire submitted; Redwood SOC2 report and pen-test summary requested.
- 2026-02-18: Procurement & Legal kickoff — provided template MSA and DPA from Redwood; Northstar legal sent redlines (focus: liability cap, data deletion timelines, subcontractor disclosure).

Requirements & priorities (from product + infra):
- Workloads: support-agent + doc-search + reranking (peak QPS ~120, typical 45).
- Latency target: p95 < 400ms for short-chat flows, p95 < 600ms for long contexts.
- Throughput: sustained 40–60 qps, spikes to 120 qps during launches.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-market budget, want predictable committed spend; exploring reserved Dedicated commit for unit economics.
- Model needs: open-model compatible; ability to pin model versions and automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants for cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Routing: multi-region failover (NA primary, EU fallback) and model routing by policy.
- Data controls: tenant isolation, KMS integration for key management, audit logs for requests and tokens, retention controls and deletion on customer request.

Legal / procurement notes (current):
- Northstar sent MSA redlines: removing broad indemnity for customer data, limiting liability tied to SLA credits, clarifying IP ownership of derivatives. Redwood legal provided counter with exceptions.
- DPA redlines: specific language on subprocessors and 30-day data deletion window after contract termination (Northstar requests 7-day).
- SLA: Northstar pushing for 99.95% for mission-critical flows; Redwood standard 99.9% for Dedicated — negotiating financial credits and a rollback plan on incidents.
- Security items outstanding: SOC2 Type II report, penetration test summary, public cloud region residency assurances for EU customers, KMS integration specifics.

Operational / onboarding items:
- Requested onboarding runbook + runbook for canary rollouts, escalation contacts, and dedicated monitoring dashboards.
- POC-to-production checklist: capacity sizing, key rotation plan, SSO/SAML provisioning, VPC peering network test, egress limits.
- Timeline: Northstar procurement wants contract signed and Dedicated onboarding started by 2026-03-31 to align with product launch window.

Quotes & call snippets:
- "We want predictability — if we commit, we need clear economics and an ops playbook for incidents." — Head of Platform (Northstar).
- "Latency is acceptable, happy with fallback guidance, need firm SLA for customer-facing workflows." — VP Product.

Next steps (owner: Priya):
- 1) Schedule legal trilateral (Redwood Legal + Northstar Legal + AE) week of 2026-02-22 to close MSA redlines.
- 2) Agree DPA deletion timeline (aim: compromise 14 days) and subprocessors list.
- 3) Finalize Dedicated pricing/commit and insert into contract (finance review).
- 4) Prepare onboarding runbook and draft SLA appendix for review.

Notes on selling approach / risks:
- Strengths: good PoC metrics, product buy-in, committed launch timeline.
- Risks: legal stalls on liability & DPA, budget re-prioritization at quarter boundary, need clear escalation path for incidents.
